16:11 -!- Filip [~Filip@230.245-136-217.adsl.skynet.be] has joined #Linux4BE
16:11 < antagonizt> hey filip
16:11 < Filip> hi folks
16:11 < bshircliffe> hi
16:11 < bshircliffe> whats up?
16:12 < Filip> keep on hacking in the free world ;-)
16:12 < Filip> trying  jal0's new monitor
16:12 < bshircliffe> great
16:30 < jal0> hey filip
16:30 < Filip> hi jal0, your monitor looks great
16:31 < jal0> thanks, still lots to do, backspace dosent seem to work as expected
16:31 < Filip> only v0.01 
16:31 < jal0> plan on implementing command history too
16:32 < Filip> search ? watch ?
16:33 < jal0> i looked at pmon, look good, but would be hard to implement. it uses nmi interrupt.
16:33 < Filip> did you try serial at higher speeds ?
16:33 < jal0> no, but should be real easy to modify.
16:34 < jal0> SetSerial(9600, EVEN_PARITY, 8, 1); in function "start"
16:34 < jal0> just change it to whatever you like
16:36 < Filip> could save some time when dumping several MB's
16:37 < jal0> the problem with creating a real monitor is that it needs some form of hardware support. so implementing say loading programs and breakpoints would be hard to do
16:38 < jal0> you would have to implement some hardware support, usually this is in the form of a nmi, where commands from the serial port interrupt the currently running program and pass control to the monitor.
16:39 < jal0> basically shorting the rx line to the nmi line of the processor works
16:40 < jal0> there are software methods but they are alot more difficult to implement and cannot be used for debugging interrupts themselves
16:41 < jal0> i'm hoping that maybe once this project get futher along, someone will donate working pda's so they can be modified to support such things. :)
16:42 < Filip> like Casio ?
16:43 < jal0> sure, would be great, but i doubt it. unless it's benificial to them, i don't see them contributing anything
16:44 < bshircliffe> I need to e-mail casiovince
16:44 < jal0> i probabbly just end up buying another one for that purpose eventually
16:47 < jal0> has anyone tried to implement the code from my serial example in the kernel? maybe we can get kgdb working.
16:47 < jal0> although i'm not sure if it requires an interrupt based serial driver or not
16:48 < Filip> I didn't try, and now that the mysterious crashes are gone have no immediate need
16:49 < jal0> filip: what would you recommend the best path of learning cvs, i don't mess with our because i don't want to screw things up.
16:49 < jal0> it would be easer that emailing people my updates
16:50 < jal0> maybe install a local cvs server and play with it?
16:51 < Filip> don't need a server to play with cvs: if you're on your local linux box
16:51 < Filip> just set your CVSROOT to something (/home/cvs) 
16:51 < jal0> i have a linux box on the network, just not my main development system

17:00 < Filip> maybe you're triggering an interupt
17:02 < jal0> AF000900

17:02 < Filip> so an interupt could restart the prog

17:03 < jal0> should=shouldn't
17:03 < Filip> your trying to peek into the cpu

17:05 < jal0> just poking around for recognizable text and such. but yes pci is my next focus, i want to get usb working
17:06 < jal0> should be easier once i get the pcb and can take a look at how the external memory map is constructed
17:07 < jal0> AF000800 should be the siu base of the vr4131
17:08 < Filip> indeed
17:08 < jal0> also poking around the AA008680 which suposedly is the vr4173 sui base, but the info there dosn't match what it should be.
17:10 < jal0> besides the fact, that the vr4173 has no siu :/
17:12 -!- bshircliffe [~bshirclif@twhou-215-38.ev1.net] has quit [Read error: 54 (Connection reset by peer)]
17:12 < jal0> btw, i think that the D89041F100 is not a chip id, rather a datecode or maybe batch number. i see the similar format id on the vr4131 chip under the actual chip id
17:13 < jal0> under=over
17:13 < jal0> http://www.linux4.be/~jroark/images/Board_bot.jpg
17:16 < Filip> and what's the other number ?
17:16 < jal0> one is a batch number the other a datecode most likely
17:18 < Filip> so no real identification ?
17:19 -!- jalo [~not@12-243-94-89.client.attbi.com] has joined #linux4be
17:19 < jalo> oops
17:21 -!- jal0 [~not@12-243-94-89.client.attbi.com] has quit [Read error: 54 (Connection reset by peer)]

17:21 -!- jal0 [~not@12-243-94-89.client.attbi.com] has joined #linux4be
17:22 < jal0> hopefully there will be some markings under the chip :)
17:24 < Filip> is that common practice  ?
17:26 < jal0> yeah
17:28 < jal0> usually when mass producing ic's not everyone is stress-tested, only a percentage in a batch are done. the batch number keeps track of this info
17:30 < jal0> there are differnet manufacturing process of course, so this is only what i believe. the date code format seems to match up with the format on the cpu. another way to check would be to look on a differnt nec component in a different product to see if the format is consistent
17:34 < jal0> http://www.pocketpcpassion.com/casio/leex/E115Overclock.htm
17:34 < jal0> ic has the same datecode format
17:35 < jal0> µPD30121
17:36 < jal0> is the part number for the 4121
17:37 < jal0> so actually, D89041F1001 *is* a part number, its µPD89041
17:38 < Filip> which is ?
17:40 < jal0> what do you mean?
17:40 < jal0> http://www.plasma-online.de/index.html?content=http%3A//www.plasma-online.de/english/identify/picture/nec_cpu.html
17:44 < jal0> VR4131(partid) = D30131F1(onchip) = µPD30131(nec part#)
17:44 < jal0> so to follow the same format
17:44 < jal0> D89041F1001(onchip) = µPDD89041(nec part#) = ?(partid)
17:44 < Filip> µPD89041== ??
17:45 < Filip> is there some logic in those  number ? like ranges for  companions, cpu's, etc
17:45 < jal0> the internal part number for the device, if you go to nec and search by id, this is the number you have to give them
17:46 < jal0> not sure yet, but still have no luck looking for a µPD89041
17:47 < jal0> or UPD89041
